@sushantdhiman Sorry for my carelessness, tested and updated this time!

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/11896237/50289205-6ccd1400-0468-11e9-9cfe-146474c03f69.png)
As this regression was introduced in v5.0.0-beta.14, it would be cool if contributors @SimonSchick @u9r52sld @tsasaki609 could review their committed PRs

Hi @frlinw ,

I reproduced the issue.

v5.0.0-beta13 output
```
Executing (default): SELECT `clientfile`.`id`, `mission`.`id` AS `mission.id`, `building`.`id` AS `building.id` FROM `clientfiles` AS `clientfile` INNER JOIN `missions` AS `mission` ON `clientfile`.`id` = `mission`.`clientfileId` AND (`mission`.`startDate` >= '2019-01-21 12:59:57.558 +00:00' AND `mission`.`startDate` <= '2019-01-21 12:59:57.558 +00:00') LEFT OUTER JOIN `buildings` AS `building` ON `clientfile`.`id` = `building`.`clientfileId`;
```

v5.0.0-beta14 output
```
Executing (default): SELECT `clientfile`.`id`, `building`.`id` AS `building.id` FROM `clientfiles` AS `clientfile` INNER JOIN `buildings` AS `building` ON `clientfile`.`id` = `building`.`clientfileId` AND (`building`.`startDate` >='2019-01-21 13:18:07.723 +00:00' AND `building`.`startDate` <= '2019-01-21 13:18:07.723 +00:00');
(node:70392) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: SequelizeDatabaseError: SQLITE_ERROR: no such column: building.startDate
    at Query.formatError (/Users/sasakitakashi/sequelize/lib/dialects/sqlite/query.js:441:16)
    at Query._handleQueryResponse (/Users/sasakitakashi/sequelize/lib/dialects/sqlite/query.js:89:18)
    at afterExecute (/Users/sasakitakashi/sequelize/lib/dialects/sqlite/query.js:269:31)
    at replacement (/Users/sasakitakashi/sequelize/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/trace.js:19:31)
    at Statement.errBack (/Users/sasakitakashi/sequelize/node_modules/sqlite3/lib/sqlite3.js:16:21)
(node:70392) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: Unhandled promise rejection. This error originated either by throwing inside of an async function without a catch block, or by rejecting a promise which was not handled with .catch(). (rejection id: 1)
```

As you say, this regression was introduced in v5.0.0-beta.14.
I will review our committed PRs.

Well, `_conformOptions` call `_conformInclude` which returns include in a consistent form. So the mess probably happens during `_.assignWith`
https://github.com/sequelize/sequelize/blob/10c34e3adf4ee281462da78f5a4a77d2d3338675/lib/model.js#L769-L774
But with that kind of code, I can't understand what is going on...
https://github.com/sequelize/sequelize/blob/10c34e3adf4ee281462da78f5a4a77d2d3338675/lib/model.js#L801-L806
@sushantdhiman as you plan to release the v5, this issue should be taged as v5, regression, bug or whatever.
